subject: government

questions.question: A key principle of democracy is that ______.

options.text: the minority may vote but the majority decides
only the majority vote is counted
an electoral college is always necessary

questions.explanation: Democracy combines majority rule with the right of the minority to participate and dissent. The majority’s decision prevails, but minority votes are counted and minority rights protected.

questions.question: Sovereignty that rests on the consent and mandate of the people is called ______.
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty locates ultimate authority in the people. Legal sovereignty locates it in the constitution or parliament.

questions.question: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to ______.

options.text: approach a court for a remedy

questions.explanation: Seeking redress means asking a court or tribunal to remedy a wrong. It is not a licence to appeal every decision or to act outside the law.

questions.question: An order compelling a lower court or public authority to perform its public duty is called ______.
questions.explanation: Mandamus requires a public body to perform a duty it has refused or failed to perform. Habeas corpus concerns unlawful detention; certiorari quashes a decision.

questions.question: A form of government whose guiding principle is “rule of the best” is ______.
questions.explanation: Aristocracy means rule by a small group regarded as the best qualified. Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy and timocracy by property owners.

questions.question: Deconcentration of power means ______.

options.text: the sharing of powers among tiers of government
the transfer of administrative authority to central-government officials stationed in the regions
the creation of semi-autonomous units to govern parts of the state
the delegation of powers to component units that already exist in the state

questions.explanation: Deconcentration shifts administrative authority from the capital to field offices of the same central government. Sharing power among tiers is federalism; transferring it to separate units is devolution.

questions.question: The independence of the judiciary means that ______.

options.text: the judiciary must not concern itself with legislative or executive affairs
court decisions cannot be reviewed by the executive
legislative and executive influence on judicial decision-making must be prevented
the dignity of judges must be preserved

questions.explanation: Judicial independence protects judges from external pressure so they decide on law and evidence. It does not mean courts never interact with the other arms; judicial review is part of the checks.

questions.question: A political party can be said to have a national outlook if ______.

options.text: it is ethnic-based but has branches across the country
it is registered by the electoral commission as a national party
it is led by people who are famous at home and abroad
its membership cuts across ethnic boundaries

questions.explanation: A national party draws members from many ethnic and regional groups. Registration or famous leaders do not by themselves give it a national character.

questions.question: Argument, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begin at the ______.
questions.explanation: The second reading is where the principle of the bill is debated. The first reading is formal introduction, the committee stage examines details, and the third reading is final approval.

questions.question: A vote of no confidence means ______.

options.text: the same thing as impeachment in a presidential system
disapproval of the government which, if carried, requires the ministers and their head to resign
the power of the head of state to dissolve parliament
disapproval of the prime minister for breaching collective responsibility

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the executive depends on the legislature’s confidence. If a no-confidence motion passes, the government resigns or seeks a dissolution and election.

questions.question: Popular political participation refers to ______.

options.text: the majority of the people holding public office
a large number of voters turning out at elections
the total activities through which citizens actively take part in political life
the efforts of more than half the citizens to join public debate

questions.explanation: Participation covers voting, campaigning, contacting officials, protesting and standing for office — not only election turnout or office-holding.

questions.question: The area from which one or more members are elected to a public office is called an electoral ______.
questions.explanation: A constituency is the electoral area represented by an elected member. An electoral college is a body that elects someone indirectly.

questions.question: Citizenship by naturalisation is ______.

options.text: the process by which a non-citizen who satisfies constitutional criteria becomes a legal member of the state
the same as citizenship by marriage and registration
the process by which an alien receives a certificate from the judiciary and becomes a citizen by birth

questions.explanation: Naturalisation is a legal process: an adult foreigner who meets residence, character and other constitutional conditions applies and takes an oath of allegiance.

questions.question: The last measure used by a pressure group when it issues a condition to be met within a fixed time is called ______.
questions.explanation: An ultimatum is a final demand with a deadline, warning of action if it is not met. Lobbying and dialogue are earlier, softer tactics.

questions.question: A form of government organised by a council of military officers is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A junta is a small group, typically military officers, ruling after seizing power. The council-of-officers form is specifically a junta.

questions.question: The non-stratified society in the pre-colonial era was that of the ______, where decisions were made by ______.
questions.explanation: Igbo society was largely acephalous: village assemblies and age grades decided issues by consensus. The Okpara headed the council of elders, but consensus characterised the system.

questions.question: The creation of twelve states was an achievement of the ______ regime.
questions.explanation: Gowon created twelve states in 1967, replacing the four regions. Murtala created seven more in 1976 and Babangida created eleven in 1987 and 1991.

questions.question: The basis of Nigeria’s foreign policy during the Independence Constitution era was ______.
questions.explanation: From independence, Nigeria put Africa at the centre of its foreign policy — decolonisation, African unity and support for liberation movements — while remaining non-aligned in the Cold War.

questions.question: The Brussels Conference of 1889–90 was primarily concerned with ______.

options.text: implementing the decisions of the Berlin Conference
planning how to penetrate Africa economically

questions.explanation: The Brussels Anti-Slavery Conference of 1889–90 focused on suppressing the slave trade, especially in Africa. The Berlin Conference (1884–85) dealt with the rules of colonial partition.

questions.question: According to Lewis Samuel, imperialism identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation is ______.
questions.explanation: Lewis Samuel Feuer distinguished progressive imperialism, which claims to spread civilisation, from regressive imperialism, which seeks conquest and exploitation for its own sake.

questions.question: One major defect of the Nigerian Council that led to its replacement was that it was ______.

options.text: able to make law only for the Southern Protectorate
less powerful than the Executive Council

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Council (1922) was largely advisory and nominated, with no elected Nigerian members, so it did not represent public opinion. It was replaced under the Richards Constitution.

questions.question: An important provision of the 1946 Constitution was that it ______.

options.text: introduced an official majority in the Legislative Council for the first time
created the office of head of government at regional level

questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 divided Nigeria into three regions and is credited with conceiving a federal structure. Full federalism with regional premiers came later, under Lyttleton (1954).

questions.question: Implementation of government programmes is the primary duty of the ______, which is part of the ______.
questions.explanation: The civil service is the permanent administrative arm that implements policy, and it is one component of the wider public service, which also includes boards, corporations and the armed forces.

questions.question: The most recent target plans and agenda of the United Nations are known as the ______.
questions.explanation: The Sustainable Development Goals (2015–2030) succeeded the Millennium Development Goals. Agenda 2063 is the African Union’s plan.

questions.question: Under the 1963 Constitution, a federal judge could be removed by ______.

options.text: a two-thirds majority of the National Assembly

questions.explanation: The 1963 Constitution required an address supported by a two-thirds majority of the federal legislature before a judge could be removed, protecting the judiciary from unilateral executive action.

questions.question: Under the 1999 Constitution, the Chief Law Officer and the head of the Supreme Court are respectively the ______.
questions.explanation: The Attorney-General of the Federation is the Chief Law Officer. The Chief Justice of Nigeria heads the Supreme Court.

questions.question: The scope of the EFCC’s duties does not extend to ______.

options.text: arresting suspects of cybercrime and online fraud
arresting both the giver and the taker in a corruption case
conducting trials and punishing persons involved in corruption

questions.explanation: The EFCC investigates and prosecutes economic and financial crimes; only courts can try and punish. That separation is itself an aspect of the rule of law.

questions.question: The Green Revolution programme was the flagship manifesto of the ______ in 1979.
questions.explanation: The National Party of Nigeria (NPN) campaigned on the Green Revolution to boost food production and won the 1979 presidential election.

questions.question: Nigeria’s federalism is often measured against the classical federal principle associated with ______.
questions.explanation: K. C. Wheare defined the federal principle as a division of powers between general and regional governments, each independent within its sphere — the benchmark used to judge Nigeria’s system.

questions.question: The most representative organ of the United Nations is the ______.
questions.explanation: The General Assembly includes all member states, each with one vote. The Security Council has limited membership and primary responsibility for peace and security.

questions.question: The Executive Council of the African Union makes decisions by ______.

options.text: a veto of the General Secretariat

questions.explanation: The AU Executive Council generally proceeds by consensus; where consensus fails, a two-thirds majority of members may decide substantive questions.

questions.question: Amendment of the United Nations Charter is the duty of the ______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 108, amendments are adopted by a two-thirds vote of the General Assembly and then ratified by member states, including all permanent members of the Security Council.
